pairs.subject: audit-logging
pairs.evidence: src/lib/db/audit-append.ts:49 The one write door (auditRowData) signs and stringifies the caller's arbitrary meta with no allowlist, secret-pattern scrub or size cap, so whatever a writer passes becomes durable, signed, exported audit evidence.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/db/audit-append.ts:49 Free-form meta is stored as-is: no allowlist, scrubber or truncation marker inside the door (searched audit-append.ts and audit-integrity.ts for sanitize/scrub/cap and found none).

src/lib/db/scans-audit.ts:28 recordAudit, claimOrgAuditOnce and releaseAuditClaim all write through appendAudit. The only direct AuditLog create/createMany calls are inside audit-append.ts, and audit-writes.contract.test.ts guards against bypasses.

src/lib/db/scans-audit.ts:33 A failed write returns false without failing the action, and it is counted in audit-health.ts and shown by AuditHealthNotice on the Audit tab. The claim path fails closed (claimed:false), as the technique's claim exception requires.

src/lib/db/audit-append.ts:90 Claim release is now a new claim.released record (good), but the door itself exports redactAuditRow, an in-place update of actorId and meta. That is a mutation surface the technique says must be absent.

src/lib/db/scans-audit.ts:388 The per-row HMAC is recomputed on every read. Verdicts are ok, tampered, unsigned or no-secret, and they appear in the API and the CSV export. The rung (per-row, no chain) is stated honestly in audit-integrity.ts.

src/lib/db/scans-audit.ts:355 Actor, action and time are structured filters, but the subject only exists inside the meta JSON string. There is no subject or outcome column or filter (AuditLogQuery has action/actorId/since/until), which is the 'facts buried in a payload blob' failure.
src/lib/db/scans-audit.ts:26 This ledger records actions the system itself performs, so one clock stamped at the door is correct.

pairs.subject: audit-logging
pairs.evidence: src/lib/db/retention.ts:1165 Erasure with the redact disposition rewrites and re-signs every stored audit row for the org in place, a targeted content mutation rather than horizon retirement. The audit horizon is also enforced by a scheduled sweep instead of at insert.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/db/retention.ts:1165 In-place update of existing ledger rows during erasure. The standard's answer is to keep personal data out at the door, not to edit history afterwards.
src/lib/db/retention.ts:1096 Personal data is scrubbed from stored rows after the fact, the failure the technique names, because nothing kept it out of meta at insert.

src/lib/db/retention.ts:405 One pooled AuditLog plus other ledgers share a single horizon, trimmed by the nightly cron (pruneAudit deleteMany) rather than the insert path. Two parts do conform: windows below the floor are refused (line 747), and the trim's self-record is written after the deletes, only when something was deleted.
src/lib/db/retention.ts:930 A lost retention.purged self-record turns the run degraded (207) instead of green.
src/lib/db/retention.ts:925 The purge audits itself through the shared recordAudit door, not a private insert.

pairs.registryProposal: Erasure against a signed, append-only ledger: the corpus says to keep PII out at the door, but gives no rule for a ledger that already holds PII when an Art.17 request arrives. This repo redacts in place and re-signs. A technique-level rule for the legacy-data case (crypto-shred vs re-signed redaction record vs supersession) would settle whether this is a deviation or the sanctioned exception.
